2015_081_061615spmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for a special meeting of the Troy Board of Education held June 16, 2015 at 5:30 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda carries three personnel items — administrative appointments of Kristine Griffor as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction and Christin Silagy as Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments, both effective July 1, 2015 — plus ratification of a one-year successor agreement with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA. The TESPA contract, running July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, carries a 1% salary schedule increase, step movement, and a 4% off-schedule payment, with an administration-stated total net increase over 2014/15 of approximately $30,000. The meeting closes with a closed session on the Superintendent Evaluation.

**Meeting**
Agenda of Special Meeting, Troy Board of Education, June 16, 2015, 5:30 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools; district site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Consent agenda items are acted on at one time unless removed.

**Agenda order**
1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Personnel (A. Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; B. Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments; C. TESPA Contract Ratification); 4. Closed Session (A. Superintendent Evaluation); 5. Adjournment.

**3.A — Administrative Appointment: Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction**
Recommendation of Ms. Kristine Griffor. She comes to Troy from Warren Woods Public Schools, where she spent the past 8 years — first as an Intervention Specialist for 3 years, then 5 years as Director of Curriculum. Before Warren Woods she spent 4 years as an English Language Arts teacher for Richmond Community Schools. Oakland University degrees: Bachelor's in teaching (2003), Master's in Reading Instruction (2005), Educational Specialist in Educational Leadership (2007). The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position, with duties beginning July 1, 2015.

**3.B — Administrative Appointment: Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments**
Recommendation of Ms. Christin Silagy. She joined the Troy School District in 2001 from Burbank Unified School District in Burbank, California, where she was a fourth grade teacher for 2 years. In 14 years with Troy she taught Science, Language Arts and English as a Second Language at Baker Middle School for 2 years, then moved to Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools as Program for Accelerated and Creative Education Resource Teacher for a year, and in 2004 moved to Morse Elementary School, where she currently serves as Elementary ELD Coordinator. Oakland University degrees: Bachelor's in Elementary Education (1999), Master's in Curriculum, Instruction and Leadership (2003), Educational Specialist in School Administration (2005). Duties begin July 1, 2015.

**3.C — TESPA Contract Ratification**
Tentative agreement reached June 5, 2015 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA), whose membership comprises paraprofessionals and skilled-trades employees. Membership ratified on June 10, 2015. Term: one year, July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016.

| Economic term | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Salary schedule | 1% across-the-Board increase, including longevity steps |
| Steps | Step movement for all eligible members |
| Off-schedule | 4% payment to tier 1 schedule members (hired prior to February 14, 2012) currently on step 5 or higher |
| Life insurance | Premium cost for an additional $20,000 in coverage for the 5 skilled trade employees |
| Work boots | $200 reimbursement for the 5 skilled trade employees |
| Stated net increase | Approximately $30,000 in new dollars over 2014/15; characterized as less than 1.5% |

A supporting memorandum dated Friday, June 12, 2015 from Larry Lobert, Interim Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, and Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, to Dr. Rich Machesky and the Board notes that part of the increase is retained as off-schedule (non-compounding) payments, and that the agreement states such payments are for 2015/16 only and are not a basis or starting point for a successor contract — preserving flexibility if the district's financial condition requires modifications. Attachments: signed Tentative Agreement and Board Resolution. Remaining language changes are described as without significant monetary impact.

**4.A — Closed Session**
Resolution to go into closed session to discuss the Superintendent Evaluation, as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c). No additional business follows other than adjournment. Roll call vote lines: Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming.

Board of Education agenda packet for a special meeting of the Troy School District held Tuesday, June 16, 2015 at 5:30 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000). The standard header notes that district information is available at www.troy.k12.mi.us, that Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and that meetings can also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The notice states that subjects to be discussed, considered, or acted upon are listed below, that items do not have to be taken in the order shown, and that items identified within the consent agenda are acted on at one time unless removed.

AGENDA STRUCTURE. The five numbered items are: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Personnel — Elementary Instruction; Grants & State Assessments; (TESPA) Contract Ratification, itemized as A. Consideration: Administrative Appointment — Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction (packet page 2), B. Consideration: Administrative Appointment — Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments (packet page 11), and C. Consideration: Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (packet page 18); 4. Closed Session — A. Consideration: Superintendent Evaluation (packet page 22); and 5. Adjournment.

ITEM 3.A — ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT, ELEMENTARY INSTRUCTION. The Superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Kristine Griffor to the position of Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction. Ms. Griffor comes to Troy from Warren Woods Public Schools, where she spent the past 8 years, serving first as an Intervention Specialist for 3 years and the remaining 5 years as Director of Curriculum. Prior to Warren Woods, Ms. Griffor spent 4 years as an English Language Arts teacher for Richmond Community Schools. She attended Oakland University, receiving her Bachelor's degree in teaching in 2003, her Master's degree in Reading Instruction in 2005, and her Educational Specialist degree in Educational Leadership in 2007. With Board approval, Ms. Griffor will begin her duties as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction effective July 1, 2015. The recommended action is acceptance of a suggested resolution (with Moved by / Supported by and Yes / No lines) reading: BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Kristine Griffor, who will begin her duties as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, effective July 1, 2015.

ITEM 3.B — ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, DIRECTOR OF ELD, FEDERAL GRANTS & STATE ASSESSMENTS. The Superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Christin Silagy to the position of Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments. Ms. Silagy came to the Troy School District in 2001 from the Burbank Unified School District in Burbank, California, where she served as a fourth grade teacher for 2 years. During her 14 years with Troy, Ms. Silagy taught Science, Language Arts and English as a Second Language at Baker Middle School for 2 years. She then moved to Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools as the Program for Accelerated and Creative Education Resource Teacher for a year. In 2004 she moved to Morse Elementary School, where she currently serves as an Elementary ELD Coordinator. Ms. Silagy attended Oakland University, receiving her Bachelor's degree in Elementary Education in 1999, her Master's degree in Curriculum, Instruction and Leadership in 2003, and her Educational Specialist degree in School Administration in 2005. With Board approval, she will begin her duties as Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments as of July 1, 2015. The suggested resolution states that the Board of Education takes action to approve the aforementioned personnel recommendation as stated above, with Moved by / Supported by and Yes / No lines.

ITEM 3.C — TESPA CONTRACT RATIFICATION. A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA) was reached on June 5, 2015. The TESPA membership, comprised of paraprofessionals and skilled-trades employees, voted to ratify the agreement on June 10, 2015. The new one-year contract is for the period commencing July 1, 2015 and ending June 30, 2016. The agreement includes a 1% increase in the existing salary schedule, step movement for all eligible members, and a 4% off-schedule payment to members on the tier 1 schedule who are currently on step 5 or higher. The agreement also includes additional language changes that do not have significant monetary impact. The suggested resolution states that the Board of Education hereby ratifies and adopts the tentative agreement reached on June 5, 2015 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA for the period of July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, with Moved by / Supported by and Yes / No lines.

SUPPORTING MEMORANDUM ON THE TESPA TENTATIVE AGREEMENT. A memorandum dated Friday, June 12, 2015 is addressed to Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent, and the Board of Education, from Larry Lobert, Interim Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, and Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, regarding the TESPA Tentative Agreement. Contact details shown on the memorandum are the Business Office, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone 248.823.4022 and fax 248.823.4013. The memorandum announces that a tentative agreement has been reached with TESPA and that it is recommended for Board action at the June 16, 2015 meeting since member ratification has occurred. It states the agreement allows for a net increase (new dollars over 2014/2015) of less than 1.5%, attributed to changes in the pay structure explained in the memorandum and outlined in the attached signed Tentative Agreement. The agreement is described as providing modest improvements to the salary structure while retaining portions of the increase as off-schedule (non-compounding) payments; a clear understanding is expressed in the agreement that such payments are for 2015/16 only and are not to be considered as a basis or starting point for a successor contract, which the memorandum says will help the district retain some flexibility if the district's financial condition requires modifications next year.

The memorandum states the total dollar net increase over 2014/15 is approximately $30,000, comprising the following economics: a 1% across-the-Board increase to the existing salary schedule, including longevity steps; step movement for all eligible members; a 4% off-schedule payment for employees on the tier 1 schedule (those hired prior to February 14, 2012) who are currently on step 5 or higher; premium costs for an additional $20,000 in life insurance coverage for the 5 skilled trade employees; and a $200 reimbursement for work boots for the 5 skilled trade employees. Readers are directed to contact either Larry Lobert or Rick West with questions, comments, or concerns. Attachments listed are the signed Tentative Agreement and the Board Resolution.

ITEM 4.A — CLOSED SESSION, SUPERINTENDENT EVALUATION. The packet notes the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss the Superintendent Evaluation, and that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, after which no additional business will take place other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The recommended action is adoption of a resolution stating that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss Superintendent Evaluation. A roll call vote is required, with named lines for Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, and Fleming. The agenda concludes with item 5, Adjournment.
